title: Tool parameter declaration format and ambiguous-field resolution
creator: Asha Menon
description: Scope: Define a compact, human-editable JSON parameter declaration format for runtime tool/function calls and a deterministic set of resolution rules for ambiguous parameter names. Deliverables: 1) Precise field DSL (types + modifiers + aliases + deprecations), 2) Validation behavior matrix (strict vs permissive/coerce), 3) Canonical error envelope and mapping to HTTP status codes, 4) Ambiguity resolution algorithm (case/format/alias precedence), 5) Telemetry events and rollout plan for backward compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: A compact JSON declaration syntax is documented with examples for common patterns (enums, nested objects, arrays).
Runtime implements name-resolution algorithm that handles snake_case/camelCase/space-separated names and respects explicit aliases/deprecated_aliases in the declaration.
Validation produces canonical error payloads containing code, human_message, param_path, and suggested_fix, stable across minor runtime releases.
A migration toggle allows permissive-coercion mode for 30 days post-release; default is strict validation after rollout window.
Telemetry exposes counters and histograms for rejected requests, successful coercions, and ambiguous-resolution occurrences.
Unit and integration tests cover at least 95% of declared behaviors and examples linked in the design doc.
design_notes: We intentionally favor a compact declaration DSL (short keys, explicit modifiers) to keep the tool authoring surface small for SDKs and internal UIs.
Trade-off: permissive-coercion improves developer UX but can mask client bugs. Plan: enable permissive mode behind a project-scoped feature flag and surface coercions in telemetry and logs.

Ambiguity resolution precedence: explicit 'name' field in incoming payload > exact match > alias match > case-insensitive match > normalized (remove punctuation/whitespace) match. Documented algorithm must be deterministic to avoid flapping.
api_examples:
Declaration example (stringified JSON for docs): '{
  "param": "user_id",
  "type": "string",
  "modifiers": ["required"],
  "aliases": ["userId", "user id"],
  "deprecated_aliases": ["uid"]
}'
Coercion example (permissive mode): incoming 'limit': "10" coerced to integer 10; telemetry event 'param.coercion' emitted with details.
error_mapping: param.missing -> HTTP 400; message: 'Required parameter {param} missing.'; user_action: 'Provide the parameter or a valid alias.'
param.type_mismatch -> HTTP 422; message: 'Parameter {param} has wrong type; expected {expected}.'; user_action: 'Coerce value or change type at client.'
param.deprecated_alias_used -> HTTP 200 (warning header); message: 'Deprecated alias {alias} used for {param}; please migrate.'; user_action: 'Switch to canonical name.'
param.ambiguous -> HTTP 400; message: 'Ambiguous parameters: matched multiple declarations.'; user_action: 'Disambiguate by using canonical names or remove duplicates.'
param.coercion_applied -> HTTP 200 (info in body) when permissive mode enabled; telemetry emitted.
telemetry: metrics: counters for failure/success per route, histogram for number of alias resolutions per request, rejection rate by client SDK version
logs: emit structured log lines with request_id, rule_version, and param resolution trace for postmortem.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spec review): Share DSL spec and examples with SDK and UX teams (1 week).
Phase 1 (implementation behind flag): Runtime implements validator + resolution algorithm behind project flag; SDKs add helper functions for alias declarations (2 sprints).
Phase 2 (canary): Enable permissive-coercion for 5% of traffic (2 weeks) and monitor telemetry for unexpected coercions/ambiguities.
Phase 3 (audit + opt-in migration): Notify clients using deprecated aliases via warning headers and dashboard reports for 30 days.
Phase 4 (strict by default): Flip default to strict validation; permissive mode remains available per-project for compatibility.
Rollout success criteria: <0.5% increase in client errors, migration notices acknowledged by key clients, no uptick in support tickets related to parameter parsing.
